title: Section 142 NI Act — Cognizance of offences

content.heading: Cognizance of offences
content.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque; such complaint is made within one month of the date on which the cause of action arises under clause (c) of the proviso to section 138 (the court may condone delay if the complainant satisfies it that he had sufficient cause); and no court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under section 138. The offence is inquired into and tried only by a court within whose local jurisdiction the cheque is drawn or delivered for collection through an account, or presented according to the applicable amended clauses. Related provisions address transfer of pending cases and single trial of offences in respect of multiple cheques.
